text: There is currently no direct scientific literature establishing Griseofulvin as a therapeutic agent for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) via the ABL1 target. Griseofulvin is primarily an antifungal agent that functions by binding to tubulin and inhibiting microtubule assembly, which leads to mitotic arrest. While some studies suggest that microtubule-targeting agents can indirectly influence signaling pathways involved in oncogenesis, there is no evidence that Griseofulvin acts as a kinase inhibitor or a modulator of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein characteristic of CML. Consequently, any proposed interaction between Griseofulvin and ABL1 in the context of CML remains speculative and lacks validation in peer-reviewed literature.
